name: Altona 1889
designer: Unidentified in the consulted historical specimen
description: Heavy condensed display letters with sloping crossbars, alternating descending terminals and a distinct historical lowercase.
observed: Directly sampled characters: 24789ABCDEFGHIKLMNOPRSTUWXYabcdefghiklmnopqrstuvy. Printed page 170, PDF page 176. Larger impressions anchor the master; smaller sizes supply additional characters.
reconstructed: Inferred companion letters and figures: JQVZjwxz01356. Punctuation and remaining symbols are new project drawings. Both cases are retained. The specimen mixes descending and plain terminal variants of several letters; this master selects one observed variant per character, without claiming a complete alternate set. Spacing and harmonisation of optical sizes are modern choices. The 1889 suffix dates the source, not a claim of first release.

sources.title: Specimen book from the Boston type foundry (1889), Altona; printed p. 170, one-based PDF page 176, Internet Archive leaf 176
sources.rights: 1889 US publication, public domain under the maximum historical 95-year term. Library of Congress scan hosted by Internet Archive; retained institutional metadata says the Library is unaware of copyright restrictions. Original native JP2 leaf; no modern digital typeface used.

revival.author: Harold Lehmann
revival.notes: Reviewed transcriptions and exact native crops are retained in source/rows.json, selections.json and tracing.json. New companions are recorded separately with construction notes.
